domain: game night snack planning for friends
base_instruction: You are a helpful party planning assistant. Help the user plan snacks for a game night by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific snack options, check each item against every active guest's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any health updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm hosting a board game night this Saturday and need help figuring out snacks. Got any ideas?

flow_info.value: Four people total: me, Derek, Megan, and Sam
Derek had a scary EpiPen incident at a Thai place last year — turned out the satay sauce got him
Sam was diagnosed celiac about a year ago so everything needs to be gluten-free when he's around
We're planning to play from around 6pm to midnight, so snacks need to be easy finger food
Sam just bailed — he's got a work emergency. But his partner Nina is still coming, she was really looking forward to it
Megan just texted me — she went to her doctor yesterday and got flagged for gestational diabetes, so she's supposed to watch her sugar intake now too
Oh also, Derek asked if his coworker Priya can come too. I said sure. She grew up in a traditional Jain household — her family is pretty devout
Should I get drinks too? I was thinking a mix of beer and sodas

Snack list to check: pad thai spring rolls with peanut dipping sauce, mini beef sliders, hummus with garlic pita chips, caprese skewers with fresh mozzarella and tomato and basil, chocolate brownies, gluten-free crackers with aged cheddar

Satay sauce → primary ingredient is peanuts
Severe peanut reaction requiring EpiPen → peanut allergy

constraints.value: Pregnant — should avoid raw fish, alcohol, and soft/fresh cheeses
inference_chain: Pregnancy restrictions → no raw fish, no alcohol, avoid soft/fresh cheeses

constraints.value: Gestational diabetes — must limit sugar intake
constraints.surface_form: Megan just texted me — she went to her doctor yesterday and got flagged for gestational diabetes, so she's supposed to watch her sugar intake now too
Sam was diagnosed celiac about a year ago

constraints.value: Jain dietary restrictions — no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including onions and garlic
constraints.surface_form: She grew up in a traditional Jain household — her family is pretty devout
inference_chain: Traditional Jain household, devout family → follows Jain dietary laws
Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain diet → also no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes)

hidden_state.value: You are hosting a board game night this Saturday for friends. You will share the guest list and their backgrounds across several turns. Plans will change — one friend drops out, a new person joins late, and one friend gets a medical update. At the end you will present a specific snack list and ask if there are any issues. You must present the exact snack list as given and ask an open-ended question about it.

You are a relaxed, easygoing host who is used to plans changing. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Derek told me...', 'Megan texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience when the guest list shifts. You treat each update as totally normal friend-group coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Four snacks have problems and one is nuanced. Pad thai spring rolls with peanut dipping sauce: peanut sauce is dangerous for Derek (severe peanut allergy — EpiPen incident from satay sauce which contains peanuts). Mini beef sliders: beef is meat, which Priya cannot eat (Jain dietary restrictions — no meat). Hummus with garlic pita chips: garlic is a root vegetable, which Priya cannot eat (strict Jain diet excludes root vegetables including garlic and onions). Caprese skewers with fresh mozzarella: fresh mozzarella is a soft cheese, which Megan should avoid (pregnancy dietary restriction). Chocolate brownies: high in sugar, which Megan needs to limit (gestational diabetes). Gluten-free crackers with aged cheddar are fine for everyone — Sam (celiac) is no longer coming so the gluten-free aspect is a bonus but not required, and aged cheddar is a hard cheese which is safe for Megan during pregnancy.
required_elements: Pad thai spring rolls with peanut dipping sauce are problematic: peanut sauce is dangerous for Derek who has a severe peanut allergy (inferred from EpiPen incident with satay sauce)
Mini beef sliders are problematic: beef is meat, which Priya cannot eat due to Jain dietary restrictions
Hummus with garlic pita chips are problematic: garlic is a root vegetable, which Priya cannot eat under strict Jain dietary practice
Caprese skewers with fresh mozzarella are problematic: fresh mozzarella is a soft cheese that Megan should avoid during pregnancy
Chocolate brownies are problematic: high sugar content conflicts with Megan's gestational diabetes restriction
Gluten-free crackers with aged cheddar are fine for everyone currently attending — agent confirms they are acceptable
forbidden_elements: Flagging any item for gluten content as a problem (Sam who has celiac is no longer coming — his constraint is removed)
Saying gluten-free crackers are problematic for any reason (aged cheddar is hard cheese, safe for pregnant Megan)
Flagging Derek as having a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy from the satay sauce incident)
Saying Priya cannot eat dairy or cheese (Jain diet restricts meat, fish, eggs, and root vegetables — not dairy)
Keeping Sam's celiac constraint active after he dropped out of the guest list
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Derek's peanut allergy inferred from an EpiPen incident with satay sauce (satay → peanuts → peanut allergy, a 3-step inference chain), (2) Megan's pregnancy inferred from 'due in March' (→ pregnant → no raw fish, no alcohol, no soft cheese), (3) Sam's celiac constraint is REMOVED when he drops out (his partner Nina replaces him with no stated restrictions), (4) Megan's constraint is UPGRADED with gestational diabetes (adds sugar restriction on top of pregnancy restrictions), (5) Priya JOINS LATE with a high-impact inferential constraint (traditional Jain household → Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including garlic and onions). At probe time, the agent must apply the CURRENT constraint state: Derek = peanut allergy, Megan = pregnant (no soft cheese) + gestational diabetes (low sugar), Priya = Jain (no meat, no root vegetables). Sam's celiac constraint no longer applies. The gluten-free crackers with aged cheddar serve as a trap — they look like they might be problematic (gluten? cheese?) but are actually fine for everyone currently attending.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
